books.title: Perennial Seller
books.author: Ryan Holiday
books.summary: Make work that lasts. Know exactly who it is for and what it does before marketing it, build an audience you own, and play the long game instead of chasing trends.

books.title: Building a StoryBrand
books.author: Donald Miller
books.summary: The customer is the hero and the brand is the guide. Use the seven-part story framework to make the message clear enough to understand in seconds.

books.title: Ogilvy on Advertising
books.author: David Ogilvy
books.summary: Advertising exists to sell. Do the research, find a big idea, and write headlines that promise a benefit with specific facts, in layouts people can actually read.

books.title: Hey, Whipple, Squeeze This
books.author: Luke Sullivan
books.summary: Never be boring or annoying. Find one simple, true idea, show it rather than explain it, write many versions, and cut every cliche.

stages.name: Strategy
stages.question: Who is this for, and what does it do for them?

stages.name: Message
stages.question: What story do we tell, with the customer as the hero?

stages.name: Big idea
stages.question: What single, simple idea will make people stop?

stages.name: Copy
stages.question: Do the words sell clearly, specifically and briefly?

stages.name: Launch and test
stages.question: How will we learn what works and keep it working?

principles.rule: Define the work in one sentence, one paragraph and one page before writing any marketing.
principles.apply: Fill in positioning.oneSentence and oneParagraph in products/<product>/messaging.json.

principles.rule: Name exactly who it is for. Something for everyone is for no one.
principles.apply: Write the audience as a specific person with a situation, not a demographic range.

principles.rule: Aim for timeless over trendy. Avoid slang, memes and references that date the work.
principles.apply: Ask of every line: will this still make sense in five years?

principles.rule: Build a platform you own (email list, community, site) so every campaign grows a lasting audience.
principles.apply: Prefer calls to action that capture a relationship (join, subscribe) alongside the sale.

principles.rule: Marketing is never finished. Keep promoting work that sells; word of mouth compounds.
principles.apply: Plan evergreen versions of each campaign, not just launch versions.

principles.rule: The customer is the hero; the brand is the guide. Talk about them more than about us.
principles.apply: Use 'you' more than 'we'.

principles.rule: Lead with what the customer wants: one clear, specific desire.
principles.apply: Fill in brandscript.character.want.

principles.rule: Name the problem on three levels: external (the practical problem), internal (how it makes them feel), philosophical (why it is just wrong). People buy solutions to internal problems.
principles.apply: Fill in brandscript.problem.

principles.rule: Show you are the right guide with empathy (we understand) and authority (we can help: results, testimonials, numbers).
principles.apply: Every campaign carries at least one proof point.

principles.rule: Give a simple plan of about three steps so buying feels safe.
principles.apply: Fill in brandscript.plan.

principles.rule: Always call to action: a direct one (buy, book) and a transitional one for people not ready yet (download, join).
principles.apply: Every format that requires a CTA must have one, starting with a verb.

principles.rule: Show the stakes (what failure costs) and paint the success (what life looks like after).
principles.apply: Fill in brandscript.failure and brandscript.success.

principles.rule: Pass the grunt test: within a few seconds people know what you offer, how it makes life better and what to do next.
principles.apply: Headline says the offer or benefit, subhead says the improvement, CTA says the next step.

principles.rule: Have a one-liner: problem, solution, result.
principles.apply: Fill in oneLiner in products/<product>/messaging.json; use it in bios, signatures and pitches.

principles.rule: Do your homework. Study the product, the customer and the competition before writing.
principles.apply: Complete the research section of the creative brief.

principles.rule: Unless the campaign has a big idea, it will pass unnoticed.
principles.apply: Write the idea in one sentence in the brief before any layout.

principles.rule: The headline does most of the work: far more people read it than the body. Make it promise a benefit.
principles.apply: Never rely on body copy to deliver the main message.

principles.rule: Put the brand name in the headline or right beside it, so skimmers still know who it is from.
principles.apply: Brand name in the headline, or the logo next to it.

principles.rule: Be specific. Facts and numbers persuade; vague superlatives do not.
principles.apply: Replace adjectives with figures, names and details.

principles.rule: News sells. If there is something new, say so in the headline.
principles.apply: Lead with what is new, free or changed when it is true.

principles.rule: Write short sentences and short paragraphs, in plain words people use.
principles.apply: Keep body sentences under about 25 words.

principles.rule: Make it easy to read. Avoid long passages in all capitals or reversed out (light text on dark), and avoid tiny type.
principles.apply: Use the colour system's text role; keep long copy dark on light.

principles.rule: Photographs outsell drawings, and captions under images are widely read. Use them to sell.
principles.apply: Every image in long-form layouts gets a caption that carries a benefit.

principles.rule: Test everything: headlines, offers, images. Keep what works and repeat it until it stops working.
principles.apply: Make two headline variants for every paid placement.

principles.rule: Every ad builds the brand image over time. Keep a consistent personality.
principles.apply: Use the voice rules in products/<product>/messaging.json and the design foundations every time.

principles.rule: Say one thing. A single-minded message beats a list of benefits.
principles.apply: If the brief has more than one main message, split it into separate pieces.

principles.rule: Find the dramatic truth about the product, the honest thing that makes it matter.
principles.apply: Root the big idea in a real fact, not an invented claim.

principles.rule: Write many headlines (dozens), then choose. The first ideas are usually everyone's first ideas.
principles.apply: Aim for at least 20 headline options per campaign before choosing.

principles.rule: Cut cliches and empty advertising words. If a competitor could sign the line, it is not good enough.
principles.apply: The checker flags common cliches; replace them with something specific.

principles.rule: Words and picture should work together, not repeat each other. Do not say what the image already shows.
principles.apply: Read the headline with the image covered and again with it visible: the pair should say more than either alone.

principles.rule: Outdoor and posters are read in seconds: one idea, one image, very few words.
principles.apply: Follow the word limits per format.

principles.rule: Never be boring and never shout. Earn attention with an idea, not exclamation marks.
principles.apply: No exclamation marks in headlines.

principles.rule: Make the product the hero of the idea, so people remember the brand and not just the joke.
principles.apply: If the ad would work for any brand, rework it.

formats.name: Billboard / large outdoor
formats.notes: One idea, one image. CTA is a short URL or handle.

formats.name: Poster (A3, A2, 18x24 in)
formats.notes: Readable from 3 m. Details (date, place, URL) go in small type.

formats.name: Event poster
formats.notes: Details must include date, time and place.

formats.name: Instagram / LinkedIn post (on-image text)
formats.notes: The caption is separate; its first line (about 125 characters) shows before 'more'.

formats.name: Instagram / Facebook story, Reel cover
formats.notes: Keep text out of the top and bottom 250 px (interface overlays).

formats.name: Carousel slide
formats.notes: First slide is the hook; last slide carries the CTA.

formats.name: YouTube thumbnail
formats.notes: Three to five big words, maximum.

formats.name: Website hero section
formats.notes: Headline: what you offer. Subhead: how life gets better. Button: the next step.

formats.name: Flyer (A5, A4)
formats.notes: Use subheads to break body copy.

formats.name: Long-copy print ad
formats.notes: Image, headline, body, then logo and CTA. Caption every image.

words.$comment: Words and phrases the copy checker flags (playbook rule W4). Lowercase. Add your own in products/<product>/messaging.json under voice.avoidWords.
cliches: take it to the next level
